_about: Fixes that were stated out loud and are therefore owed (AGENTS.md rule 0a). Each one carries a command that PROVES it, so 'done' is never a claim. `node tools/promises.mjs` runs them all. An unkept promise is a bug, not a preference, and does not need re-approval to keep.

promises.promise: No film is rendered with the box character. The finished film uses the modular paper character.
promises.why: Three character systems existed and every film used the worst one, so back pleats, cloth drag, the kasa, the angular mask and the paper blotting were all invisible in anything anyone watched. The first version of this check only grepped for a file, which is why three films still went out with boxes on 25 Nov after the problem was written down that morning.
promises.evidence: `npm run film` is tools/film.mjs, which exports the canonical timeline and renders through blender/film_modular.py with the modular character. Every finished film writes output/<name>.render.json naming the character system that made it; the check reads those files, so a film rendered with boxes is caught by its own output and not by a grep. The boxes survive behind --preview, labelled a storyboard, and a preview writes a sidecar that says so.

promises.promise: No frame of any film puts a joint past its limit.
promises.why: The anime dial put the head 53 degrees back, past hx's own limit, and the film still validated because only authored keys were checked.

promises.promise: The hakama is pleated behind as well as in front.
promises.why: Orbit is the most-used camera at 71.4 screen-seconds and it circles the character; the back and side were the two angles it looked at most.

promises.promise: A raised arm must not bury the character's head in its own sleeve.
promises.why: At an overhead sword raise the tamoto swallowed the head and hat entirely. The pose was correct (rsx -1.63 is a real jodan); the sleeve followed the arm rigidly because tamoto_wide was skinned to lE/lS/lT and had no bone of its own.
promises.evidence: Two fixes, one per character system, each measured rather than argued. ENGINE (engine/figure.js hangCloth): the sleeve is pushed away from the body's centre line as the arm rises, it gathers up the arm, and the blend back toward the forearm fades out; worst hem clearance in the test poses went 0.4 cm -> 8.5 cm. BLENDER: a real sleeve bone per side (lSleeve/rSleeve, parented to the forearm), aimed at the ground every frame by Rig._hang_sleeves(), plus a new 'hang' skinning mode - a kimono sleeve is SEWN to the body at the shoulder and hangs free below, which inverse-distance weighting cannot express, so the top stays with the clavicle and the bottom obeys the sleeve bone. Worst face clearance over five raised-arm poses went -2.2 cm (cloth inside the face) to +2.9 cm clear; jodan-raise went -2.2 -> +13.4 cm. Bones 23 -> 25; reg.TAIL lets a childless bone state its own tail so the skin weights follow the cloth and not the arm. Only the WIDE sleeve hangs: the measurement showed tamoto_narrow, the tight fighting sleeve, already cleared the face by 0.7 cm and got WORSE when hung, so it stays skinned to the arm, which is what a cut-down sleeve is for. Both recipes validate 433/433 and 862/862.

promises.promise: The kimono has a back seam and shoulder yoke, so the torso is not one flat slab from behind.
promises.why: Found by the turnaround test; still visible in docs/PHASE1-VERDICT.md.
promises.evidence: Back seam added at CORE_OUTLINE (0.0, 1.13), the spine. Validator rose 427->433 and 856->862 checks, all passing.

promises.promise: Landings, skids and dashes mark the ground.
promises.why: analyseGround already emits land/skid/dash/wake with position, direction and speed. Only dust listens. Cheapest large win in the repo.
promises.evidence: makeGroundMarks() listens for land and skid; dash-test makes 2 marks (1 land, 1 skid). Dashes already had a wake line.
